svg.title: ADS-B AR flight tracker event-driven architecture
svg.desc: Event-driven architecture: Raspberry Pi ground station receives ADS-B aircraft messages, decodes them into flight objects, and publishes MQTT events to IBM Watson IoT Platform. iOS app subscribes, receives flight update messages asynchronously, converts to FlightInfo/FlightAnnotation, and updates AR or map view. Producer and consumer decoupled through MQTT event channel.

g.onclick: sendPrompt('How do aircraft broadcast ADS-B signals?')
g.text: Broadcast ADS-B signals on 1090 MHz — position · altitude · speed · callsign
Event producer — Raspberry Pi ground station
Receives raw ADS-B frames · decodes · publishes MQTT events

g.onclick: sendPrompt('How does the Raspberry Pi receive ADS-B signals?')
sendPrompt('How are raw ADS-B frames decoded into flight objects?')
sendPrompt('How does the ground station publish MQTT events?')
sendPrompt('How does IBM Watson IoT Platform relay MQTT flight events?')
g.text: IBM Watson IoT Platform — MQTT broker
Relay flight update messages · topic routing · decouples producer from consumer
Subscribes to MQTT · receives flight update messages asynchronously

g.onclick: sendPrompt('How does the iOS app parse incoming MQTT flight messages?')
sendPrompt('What is a FlightAnnotation in the iOS AR app?')
sendPrompt('How does the iOS app update AR and map views with flight data?')

svg.text: Producer and consumer fully decoupled — connected only through MQTT flight event channel
